## Natural history notes

A crustose lichen characterized by a thin gray to pale greenish thallus with reddish, rash-like patches or stains and tiny embedded dark fruiting bodies. In Florida, it is found growing tightly on smooth tree bark in humid wooded habitats such as hammocks, swamps, mangroves, shaded forests, parks, and other moist subtropical areas. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air while using bark mainly as a surface for attachment rather than as food.
